cards.front: If you run java Main with no arguments, is args null?
cards.extra: The JVM always passes a real array. Reading args[0] then throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, not NullPointerException.

cards.front: Does args[0] hold the program name, as in C's argv[0]?
cards.back: No — args[0] is the first real argument; Java passes no program name
cards.extra: java Main hello gives args.length == 1 and args[0] == "hello". In C the same command gives argc == 2.

cards.front: Are command-line arguments numbers when you type digits?
cards.back: No — they are always String; converting is your job
cards.extra: java Main 42 gives "42". Use Integer.parseInt(args[0]) and be ready for NumberFormatException.

cards.front: In java -Dmode=fast Main a b, what does args contain?
cards.back: Only ["a", "b"] — -D is a JVM property, not a program argument
cards.extra: Everything before the class name configures the JVM (System.getProperty); everything after goes to main.

cards.front: How do you pass an argument that contains spaces?
cards.back: Quote it in the shell — Java receives one element, not several
cards.extra: java Main "hello world" gives args.length == 1. The JVM does no splitting of its own; the shell already did.

cards.front: Can main be declared with varargs instead of an array?
cards.back: Yes — main(String... args) is the same method after erasure
cards.extra: The launcher finds it because the erased signature matches String[]. Only the source form differs.

cards.front: What is the difference between null and an empty string?
cards.back: null means no object at all; "" is a real String of length 0
cards.extra: Calling any method on null throws NullPointerException; calling length() on "" returns 0.

cards.extra: This is the classic reason to put the constant on the left, or to normalise null to empty early.

cards.front: What is the difference between isEmpty() and isBlank()?
cards.back: isEmpty checks length 0; isBlank (Java 11) also treats whitespace-only strings as blank
cards.extra: " " is not empty but is blank — the distinction matters when validating user input.
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::01 Foundations::09 Strings and Methods

cards.front: What is the difference between a null collection and an empty one?
cards.back: An empty collection is safe to iterate, size and stream; a null one throws NullPointerException
cards.extra: Return Collections.emptyList() instead of null so callers never need a check.

cards.front: What is the difference between a null array and an empty array?
cards.back: new int[0] has length 0 and can be iterated; null throws on .length
cards.extra: Empty arrays are the safe default for "no elements" — same reason empty collections are.

cards.front: What is Optional.empty() for, compared with null?
cards.back: It is an explicit, typed "no value" that callers must handle, instead of a silently missing null
cards.extra: optional.isPresent() is checked by reading the code; a null return is invisible until it explodes.
